title: Introduction to $q$-Geometric Langlands
html:
The substrate parameter q \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(k) = k^\times \setminus \mu_\infty (substrate parameter) endows the differential calculus of a quantum observable universe with a one-parameter deformation. Two consequences govern this chapter:

  1. The q-deformed exterior derivative satisfies d_q^2 \neq 0 (non-vanishing of d_q^2). This non-vanishing canonically obstructs the flatness of q-connections.
  2. The obstruction classes \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) (quantum characteristic classes) control the lifting of Frobenius--Hopf objects through the brane tower. Their Kummer filtration (Kummer filtration) isolates the arithmetic locus where q-flatness holds.

These structures assemble into a q-deformed Geometric Langlands correspondence. This equivalence is constructed as a \mathbb{G}_m-family of functors. The automorphic side consists of q-\mathcal{D}-modules on the moduli of G_q-bundles. The spectral side consists of quasi-coherent sheaves on the moduli of q-local systems for the Langlands dual \check{G}_q. The rigid fibre functor \tau (fibre-functor rigidity) mediates the equivalence via Tannaka--Krein reconstruction. This family is well-defined on the non-torsion locus \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}} but degenerates at roots of unity where [n]_q = 0. The perpetual obstruction (Kummer filtration) ensures the correspondence remains intrinsically non-torsion.
